newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Even Swedish EU-advocates against EMU - poll.
newsitem.headline: Even Swedish EU-advocates against EMU - poll.

text.p: An opinion poll showed on Friday that even those Swedes who support membership in the European Union are against joining the Economic and Monetary Union (EMU).

The poll, conducted by a Swedish research group for society and information studies (FSI), found only 18 percent of Swedish EU-advocates saw anything positive in a common European currency. A total of 52 percent said this was a bad idea.
Asked if a referendum should be held on whether Sweden should join EMU, 50 percent of the 1,137 Swedes surveyed answered yes.
Twenty-one percent did not want a referendum, 20 percent were unsure and nine percent did not know, according to the report published in daily newspaper Dagens Nyheter.

A recent poll commissioned by the European Commission showed that almost one in every two Swedes believed the country has lost out so far from membership in the European Union (EU) and that the country should pull out.
Sweden joined the EU in January 1995.
